(ORAL)
14.08.2024 1) In terms of CRM(M) No.492/2024, the petitioner has challenged FIR No.22/2024 for offences under Section 420, 403, 405, 463, 464, 468, 34 and 120-B IPC registered with Police Station,
Bemina, Srinagar.
Challenge has also been thrown to order dated 03.05.2024 passed by learned Special Mobile Magistrate (Railway Magistrate), Srinagar, pursuant whereto, the impugned FIR has been registered.

Besides this, the petitioner has also thrown challenge to order dated 07.08.2024,
whereby learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class (3rd Additional Munsiff), Srinagar, has dismissed his bail application.
2) In terms of Bail App No.82/2024, Mrs. Bilquees Akhter, Fida Mohammad Najar and Rameez Ahmad Najar, have sought bail in anticipation of their arrest in the aforesaid FIR.

sentences.text: Mr. Shakeel Sarwar Wani, respondent No.2, who is present in person, accepts notice.
5) Let reply/response be filed by the next date of hearing.
6) I have heard learned counsels for the parties on the question of grant of interim relief.

7) From a perusal of the contents of the impugned FIR, it appears that there was a transaction with regard to purchase of immovable property between complainant/respondent No.2 and main accused Shri Haji John Mohammad Dar.

As per the contents of the impugned FIR, respondent No.2 is alleged to have paid an amount of Rs.75 lacs to said Haji John Mohammad Dar through various bank transactions in his own name and in the name of petitioners in Bail App No.82/2024 but despite repeated representations and assurances on the part of the accused persons, neither the property has been transferred in the name of complainant/respondent No.2 nor the amount seems to have been refunded to him.

On the basis of these allegations, respondent No.2 has filed a detailed complaint against the petitioners and co-accused making allegations regarding fraud, deception,
criminal breach of trust and forgery on their part.

These allegations run into 43 paras and on the basis of these allegations, pursuant to the impugned order passed by the learned Mobile Magistrate,
Srinagar, on 03.05.2024, the impugned FIR has been registered.

It has come to the fore that petitioner Sheikh Abdul Majeed has been taken into custody by the police during investigation of the case and when he approached the Court of Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class (3rd Additional Munsiff),
Srinagar, his bail application was rejected on 07.08.2024.
8)

Srinagar

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that the transaction with regard to the sale/purchase of the land is essentially between respondent No.2 and main accused Haji John Mohammad Dar and the petitioners have been unnecessarily roped in the impugned FIR.

It has been contended by learned counsel appearing for petitioner Sheikh Abdul Majeed that as per the allegations made in the impugned FIR, he has only introduced respondent No.2 to main accused Haji John Mohammad Dar and for this reason only, it cannot be termed that he has conspired with the main accused, particularly when respondent No.2 has not paid any money to the said petitioner nor is he the executant/witness to the agreement to sell entered into by respondent No.2 with the main accused.

It has been further contended that the dispute, if any, between respondent No.2 and the main accused is purely of civil nature, regarding which respondent No.2 has already filed a suit before the civil court and, as such, he cannot take resort to criminal proceedings in order to coerce the petitioners to settle a purely civil dispute.

The learned counsel has also contended that while dismissing the bail application of petitioner Sheikh Abdul Majeed, the learned Magistrate has fallen into a grave error by terming the dispute between the parties as one affecting the economy of the nation and categorizing the alleged offence as an economic offence.
Sheikh Abdul Majeed vs Union Territory Of J&K & Anr on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83646276/
2 9) Respondent No.2, appearing in person, has submitted that petitioner Sheikh Abdul Majeed has all along been associated with the transaction between him and the main accused and he has always been in knowledge of the monetary transactions that have taken placed between respondent No.2 and the main accused.

entities.text: Sheikh Abdul Majeed vs Union Territory Of J&K & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has further contended that it is petitioner Sheikh Abdul Majeed who has been instrumental in striking a deal between respondent No.2 and the main accused, therefore, he cannot be absolved from his criminal liability.

He has also contended that so far as the petitioners in Bail App No.82/2024 are concerned, respondent No.2 has transferred money in their accounts on the asking of the main accused, which clearly shows that they are part of the larger conspiracy which is yet to be investigated into by the investigating agency.

10) Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the material on record, it appears that the allegations made in the impugned FIR, prima facie, disclose commission of cognizable offences.

Whether said offences are made out against petitioner Sheikh Abdul Majeed or not, this Court would not like to comment on that aspect of the matter at this stage but one thing is clear that, prima facie, offences of cognizable nature are constituted against main accused Haji John Mohammad Dar.
In these circumstances, it would not be appropriate to stay investigation of the case at this stage.

However, having regard to the nature of allegations made in the impugned FIR against petitioner Sheikh Abdul Majeed and the peripheral nature of role which has been ascribed to him in the entire transaction, a case for grant of interim indulgence in his favour is made out.

11) Accordingly, it is provided that investigation in the impugned FIR may go on but in case the investigating agency intends to file challan against petitioner Sheikh Abdul Majeed, the same shall not be done without prior permission of this Court.

It is further provided that petitioner Sheikh Abdul Majeed shall be enlarged on interim bail till next date of hearing subject to the following conditions:
(i) That he shall furnish personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/ with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Investigation Officer concerned (ii) That he shall appear before the Investigating Agency, as and when required, for purposes of investigation of the case.
(iii) That he shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence.

Having regard to the fact that petitioner Mrs.
Bilquees Akhter is a lady, it is directed that in the event of her arrest FIR No.22/2024 for offences under Section 420, 403, 405, 463, 464, 468, 34 and 120-B IPC registered with Police Station,
Bemina, she shall be released on interim bail till next date of hearing subject to the 1.

3 2.

3. That she shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence.

4. That she shall not leave the territorial limits of Union Territory of J&K, without permission of the Investigating Officer 13) The grant of bail to other petitioners shall be considered after the reply is filed by the respondents.
14) List both the petitions on 31.08.2024.
